exclusion_detail: The abstract names groups of compounds (activators 3-5, 16, 19 with EC50 1.18-1.91 nM; inhibitors 6, 11, 14, 18 with IC50 1.26-1.38 nM) but no single best or lead compound, and there is no follow-up experiment (no in vivo, docking or mechanism work) on any one of them. The numerically most potent activator is 5 (EC50 1.18 nM) but the paper does not call it the lead, so the lead rule is not applied.

lead.label: none
lead.why: Abstract: 'derivatives 3-5, 16 and 19 presented significant activation potency ... EC50 values in the range of 1.18-1.91 nM. Derivatives 6, 11, 14 and 18 showed significant inhibitory potency'; no single compound featured.

notes: Derivatives 15-21 are one step (Sc(OTf)3 Pechmann condensation of pyrogallol with a ketoester, general procedure 3.2.3) from commercial reagents. Derivatives 1-14 are one step from daphnetin, but daphnetin was supplied as a natural product isolated from Daphne giraldii root bark by a collaborating university (not purchased), so I did not list them. Compound 22 is two steps from pyrogallol (via 16). Compound 5 (hexanoyl diester, EC50 1.18 nM) would be the numerically best if a looser lead rule were used. Source: main text only; no SI file.
